My Deltarune

I love toby fox, I loved Undertale, but deltarune just doesnt interest me at all. 

Besides the addition of benefitting from near-misses while dodging, the turn based combat is minimally different, and if anything attacks are easier than in Undertale. 

As expected, the characters are cool, the world is interesting, and the vibes certainly are there... but I think the novelty and kind of "primitive" aesthetic that Undertale had isnt there (which makes sense, considering toby likely has more tools to create deltarune after undertale's success). I've played through about halfway through chapter 3, and stuff that happened in chapter 1 or 2 doesnt seem to matter anymore. Also, there's a SIGNIFICANT amount more character text reading in this. If undertale was a comic book, this game is a novel. 

i'll barely even talk about the fan base or the hype, but even if this game was PERFECT, its WAY overglazed. people talk about deltarune like it's the jesus christ of video games, and love to get upset when you bring up a genuine criticism.

Ultimately, probably not a bad game. i'll try it again after the whole game is out, but until then, its a 'no' from me.

Going by chapters:

1. Slow start, but generally solid.
2. My least favorite mainly because it triggered severe migraines due to the contrast in the environment (mostly the scenery and neon palette with strobing/sparkle effects), I wish there was some sort of photosensitivity mode. There wasn't anything else that upset me.
3. Much more enjoyable than chapter 2. I felt entertained, and had a good time. There was a moment when the chapter boss became a little bit boring/repetitive.
4. I found the runback to the last boss very annoying, the boss itself not so much.
5. The final boss has a lot of visuals that were bordering on triggering photo-sensitive migraines. I think there needs to be an option or a tweak, due to the high contrast of the bullets and objects. I struggled mainly due to this.

In general, I think it's a good game, but if you struggle with high contrast areas (think cyberpunk type colorations), you might want to sit this one out. Bit of a shame, because the rest of the game is actually really nice.

Undertale meant a lot to me after I played it as a teenager. It showed me a charming, lovable, deeply human and deeply flawed set of characters in a sometimes beautiful, sometimes whimsical, sometimes intimidating and sometimes heartbreaking underground world. It shaped me as a fan of indie games and cemented itself as one of my favorite games of all time.

This game is better.

And it isn't even freakin' done yet. 

Deltarune is a mind-boggling progression of everything that made Undertale great, times a factor of at LEAST six. Hyperbole aside, this game is everything I possibly could've wanted as a spiritual successor to one of my favorite games from my high school years, and I am deeply, utterly engrossed into everything about its world, characters, storytelling, emotions and everything else, including some moments that make me want to tear up by just thinking about them. This game is a part of my soul now, man. Toby Fox is a wizard. 

Buy it ten times.

As someone who loved Undertale, I have to admit I was a little bit skeptical that Toby Fox could recapture that magic that took over my teenage years, and so I avoided this game for several years, thinking to myself that there was no way it was really as good as people said.

That being said, I cannot think of any other game that had me genuinely burst out in laughter as many times as I have playing these chapters of DELTARUNE. I have also never felt as strong an emotional connection to video game characters as I do Kris, Susie and Ralsei. Their experiences feel real, their struggles palpable and something that I can relate to. The game might not be the most visually appealing to everyone, but if there's one thing Toby and his team understand better than any other game studio, that is character writing.

For all its humorous moments, emotional and feeling vulnerabilities, and random dog encounters; Please, give this game a try. You won't regret it.
